source_document: IFRC DREF MDRSL006 EPoA; date of disaster 5-6 September 2015
description: IFRC MDRSL006: sustained rain from 5-6 September 2015 (48 hours) burst river banks and caused destruction in eight communities in Bo District. SLRCS evacuated families from Kpahn community to Falah community. Other seven Bo communities were not named. Coordinates not published.
evidence_text: Sustained heavy downpour of rain from the 5 to the 6 September 2015 (48 hours) burst river banks and caused destruction in eight communities in Bo. SLRCS staff and volunteers based in Bo District have already started evacuating families affected by the floods from Kpahn community to Falah community.

source_document: IFRC DREF MDRSL006 EPoA; date of disaster 5-6 September 2015
event_location_name: Pujehun District (two unnamed communities in one chiefdom)
description: IFRC MDRSL006: the 5-6 September 2015 rains caused destruction in two communities in one chiefdom in Pujehun District (272 people / 41 households / 16 houses). Community names were not published. Not exploded into invented settlement rows. Not matched to Pujehun Town.
evidence_text: Sustained heavy downpour of rain from the 5 to the 6 September 2015 (48 hours) burst river banks and caused destruction in eight communities in Bo and two in one Chiefdom in Pujehun District. Pujehun District has 272 persons affected by floods with 41 household heads affected losing 16 houses.

source_document: Copernicus EMSR222 / UN-SPIDER: Freetown mudflow and floods, event time 2017-08-14
description: UN-SPIDER and Copernicus EMSR222 identify Lumley among the worst-hit Freetown areas on 14 August 2017 alongside Regent. Flash floods also reported in other unnamed capital-area communities; those unnamed places are not invented as extra events.
evidence_text: Heavy rainfall caused deadly flooding and mudslides in and around Freetown. The worst hit areas reportedly are the coastal suburb of Racecourse as well as Lumley and Regent on the outskirts of Freetown, where a hillside collapsed on Monday morning (14 August 2017).

source_document: NDMA: Freetown flood mitigation note, 24 Oct 2022, citing 28 August floods at Water Street, Wellington
description: NDMA: during the 28 August 2022 floods in Freetown, Water Street in Wellington was among the hardest hit. Same dated Wellington observation as IFRC MDRSL013; must merge, not double-count.
evidence_text: The team started with Water Street, Wellington in the East End of Freetown, where a major waterway that usually gets flooded within the community was cleared. During the August 28th floods in Freetown, Water Street was amongst the hardest hit.

evidence_text: The NDMA team then proceeded to Lower Kuntolor, where eight mud-brick homes were destroyed by floodwaters from uncontrolled hillside waterways. More than 150 people across 30 households were displaced.

source_document: NDMA risk assessment in six Western Area communities, 8 July 2024
event_location_name: Congo Town / Kolloh Town / Gray Bush and other Western Area communities
description: NDMA assessed flooding damage after a series of incident reports around 8 July 2024. Names Congo Town, Kolloh Town, Gray Bush, Pamarokor, Calaba Town, Bottomoku, Wellington and Portee, but does not publish a calendar day for the flood itself. Calaba Town is not converted into a catalog match without an event date. Held out.
evidence_text: Following a series of incident reports on damage caused by flooding due to continuous heavy rain in Freetown, NDMA embarked on a rigorous risk assessment. Flooding affected 200 households in Congo Town, Kolloh Town, and Gray Bush.
hold_out_reason: Named places without an exact flood calendar day.

source_document: IFRC MDRSL006 final report; ONS totals as of 5 October 2015
event_location_name: Freetown, Bonthe and Port Loko (2015 expansion, no community-day list)
description: MDRSL006 later expanded to Freetown, Bonthe and Port Loko with ONS totals as of 5 October 2015. The original dated disaster (5-6 September) named Bo and Pujehun only. Freetown/Bonthe/Port Loko expansion lacks a community-level calendar day and is held out.
evidence_text: Since early September 2015, Bo, Bonthe, Freetown, Port Loko and Pujehun experienced flooding. As of 5 October 2015 ONS totals: Bo 3,293; Bonthe 4,650; Port Loko 1,510; Freetown 14,050; Pujehun 800.
hold_out_reason: No exact community-level event date for the expansion districts.
